messages:
Lina (Support): Samir from Acme reported repeated 429s on their Dedicated pool during a nightly batch. Claims bursts used to be tolerated for ~90s but now they hit hard caps. Posting logs he sent.
Samir (Customer): Here's the error snippet they get:
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rw-rate-limit: 100/60
x-rw-rate-remaining: 0
x-rw-rate-reset: 167
{"error":"rate_limited","retry_after":167}
```
Samir (Customer): They say traffic is the same as last week; only difference is they rolled a larger multi-request job at 02:00 UTC. They expected reserved pool to absorb it.
Lina (Support): Adding @Jordan + @Mira to check whether reserved-pool burst window config changed or if quota accounting got stricter. Customer account id: acct-ACM-9987. Attached request traces (short IDs: rtr-11a, rtr-11b).
Jordan (Eng-Platform): Thanks. First pass: looks like the pool's burst budget is depleted rapidly. Can you paste the reserved pool config? particularly window_seconds and burst_tokens.
Mira (SRE): OpsBot run: /pool show acct-ACM-9987
OpsBot: pool: acct-ACM-9987 | capacity=1200 rps | reserved=true | burst_tokens=7200 | window_seconds=60 | refill_rate=1200
Jordan (Eng-Platform): Huh — window_seconds=60. Customer expects smoothing across 5 minutes. If their job sends many short-lived parallel requests, 60s window will surface as a hard cap much sooner than a 5m window. That explains 429s at ~02:00.
Samir (Customer): Is that a change on our side? We didn't modify anything. Did Redwood change defaults?
Lina (Support): We didn't change customer's explicit pool. But we did push a platform change last night that tightened burst accounting for multi-req sequences (to avoid token double-counting). @Jordan, could that be the deploy that affected refill behavior?
Jordan (Eng-Platform): I see a deploy at 2273010000 that included token-bucket refactor that prevents concurrent request duplication in bucket refills. It made accounting stricter (correct), but reduced effective burst headroom for some workloads. This matches.
Mira (SRE): Short-term mitigation: set window_seconds=300 for acct-ACM-9987 or temporarily increase burst_tokens by x3. Longer term: we need a customer-facing knob for "smooth burst window" vs "strict accounting". Lina, can you propose both options to the customer?
Lina (Support): I'll propose two fixes:
- Immediate: increase window_seconds to 300 for their pool (non-disruptive) or bump burst_tokens to 20000 for the nightly job window.
- Medium: schedule a config toggle for backward-compatible smoothing or provide guidance to parallelize less aggressively.
Samir (Customer): Please do the immediate increase. We'll accept manual change while we evaluate job pacing.
Jordan (Eng-Platform): Before changing, share repro steps so we can run in staging and validate rate headers. Quick reproducer (curl):
```
for i in {1..500}; do curl -s -w "\n%{http_code} %{time_total}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate?model=rw-large" &
done; wait
```
Jordan (Eng-Platform): That will show the 429 spike if window_seconds is 60.
Mira (SRE): I'll queue the config change: window_seconds=300 for acct-ACM-9987 during their 01:50-02:10 window for tonight. If that clears, we can leave 300 as baseline for scheduled batch windows.
Lina (Support): Noting customer consent. I'll inform Samir when change is live and collect post-change traces.
Samir (Customer): Thanks, appreciate the fast turnaround. Also: can you expose the pool window_seconds in the Console UI? Our infra team wants visibility.
Lina (Support): Noted as feature request to Product (I'll file a ticket). Closing loop when I have validation logs.
Jordan (Eng-Platform): Follow-up: we'll add a monitoring alert rule that flags sudden 429 spikes in Dedicated pools tied to recent platform deploys to catch regressions earlier.
Mira (SRE): Logged runbook entry: if sudden 429s for dedicated pool, check (1) pool.window_seconds, (2) burst_tokens, (3) recent deploys modifying token accounting.
Lina (Support): Change scheduled for 2273014400. I'll update thread after verification.
OpsBot: Config change applied for acct-ACM-9987 at 2273014400 by ops-runner. window_seconds: 60 -> 300
Lina (Support): Samir — please run your job again when ready and paste new x-rw-rate-* headers. Thank you.
Samir (Customer): Ran the job at 2273014488. New headers look good, no 429s. x-rw-rate: 1200/300, x-rw-rate-remaining: 1190. Looks smooth.
Lina (Support): Marking this resolved for now. We'll follow up on console visibility and monitoring alert. :white_check_mark:
